issues.display_title: Issue #1799: cc_logs.amount logs 100x too small on token/overlay/moderation success (stripe + paypal)
issues.main_description_html:
Task

insertCCLog() in BuyTokenHelpers, UnlockOverlayHelpers, and UnlockModerationHelper builds one shared $logParams['amount'] from tax_info.total (dollars) for both success and failure branches.

  • logFailedPayment() expects dollars — correct as-is.
  • logSuccessPayment() expects cents and divides by 100 (PaymentHelpers.php:64) — so every successful stripe/paypal token purchase, overlay unlock, and moderation unlock logs cc_logs.amount 100x too small (e.g. $14 recorded as $0.14).

Implementation

In all three helpers, override amount to cents via the existing PaymentHelpers::amountToCents() helper on the success branch only, right before building the LogSuccessPayment DTO:

if ($errorMessage === '') {
    $logParams['amount'] = $this->paymentHelpers->amountToCents($preparedData['tax_info']['total']);
    // ... existing transaction_id / source_id / note2 assignments

Files:

  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Helpers/OneTimePayment/BuyTokenHelpers.php (insertCCLog, ~line 124)
  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Helpers/OneTimePayment/UnlockModerationHelper.php (insertCCLog, ~line 289)
  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Helpers/OneTimePayment/UnlockOverlayHelpers.php (insertCCLog, ~line 431 — use $taxInfo['total'] ?? 0, matches surrounding style)

Do NOT touch the failure branch — it already passes dollars and logFailedPayment() stores them unchanged.

Reference pattern: UnlockPublishHelpers, UnlockPublishBlueLineHelpers, UnlockStitchingHelpers already do this correctly (success uses cents, failure uses dollars).

Out of scope: subscription upgrade/downgrade cc_logs path (UpgradeHelper::logToCCLogs, DowngradeHelper, SubscriptionHelpers) — separate pipeline, calls addEntry() directly with dollar amount, no divide. Leave untouched.

Verification

  • Buy tokens via Stripe and PayPal → cc_logs.amount equals charged dollar amount.
  • Unlock overlay via Stripe and PayPal → cc_logs.amount correct.
  • Unlock moderation via Stripe and PayPal → cc_logs.amount correct.
  • Trigger a failed purchase on each of the 3 flows → failure cc_logs.amount still logs dollar amount unchanged.

issues.display_title: Issue #1789: Add `enc` request header to toggle response encryption (default: true)
issues.main_description_html:
Background

Every endpoint that wraps its response through HelperClass::encryptResult() or ResponseEnvelopeHelper::encryptResult() always encrypts data (AES-256-CBC) before sending it to the client. Full list of the 193 affected endpoints: docs/ENCRYPTED_API_ENDPOINTS.md.

Request

Add a request header enc to toggle response encryption per-request:

  • Header absent or enc: true → current behavior, response stays encrypted (default, non-breaking).
  • enc: false → response sent without encryption, data becomes plain JSON (structure {statusCode, data: {messages, ...}} stays the same, just the cry/ciphertext field replaced with raw data).

Suggested approach

  • ResponseEnvelopeHelper already has responseMessages() (plaintext envelope) as the counterpart to encryptResult() — just branch on $request->header('enc') at that same point, no new method needed.
  • HelperClass::encryptResult() doesn't have a plaintext version yet; needs one added (or accept a flag) to reach parity with ResponseEnvelopeHelper.
  • Cheapest place to branch: inside both helpers themselves (accept Request or a bool flag), not per-controller — avoids touching ~190+ call sites individually.

Acceptance criteria

  • enc header read at the helper layer (HelperClass::encryptResult, ResponseEnvelopeHelper::encryptResult).
  • Default (header absent / enc: true) — no behavior change, stays encrypted.
  • enc: false — data is plain, statusCode & messages stay consistent with the encrypted version.
  • Applies to every endpoint in docs/ENCRYPTED_API_ENDPOINTS.md, not just a subset.
  • Update docs (docs/ENCRYPTED_API_ENDPOINTS.md or REGISTERED_APIS.md) to describe the enc header.

Ref: docs/ENCRYPTED_API_ENDPOINTS.md

issues.display_title: Issue #1800: [Investigation + Quick Fix] PayPal capture: cc_logs/cc_purchase missing entries on upgrade (user 29546)
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

A PayPal subscription payment succeeded on PayPal's side, but local DB writes stopped halfway: user_extra_data/users were updated, while cc_logs + cc_purchase + invoice were never written. There is no PayPal webhook / retry / reconciliation mechanism, so this gap stays permanent without manual repair.

Case data (user 29546 — femiomomo@gmail.com)

  • Aug 21, 2026: previous Agency subscription via Stripe (sub_1RnZ0d4UXotNjjkI6dqA45IR) stopped (monthly charge ~22nd did not run; last one Jul 12, $75)
  • Aug 22, 2026 02:59 UTC: PayPal sub I-E1WXUVCTDW1R ACTIVE (plan P-7GL25033FK647912VNF43F3I)
  • Aug 22, 2026 03:25 UTC: payment $75 COMPLETED, transaction ID 1G49172999430860H
  • DB state before repair:
    • ✅ recurring_profile = I-E1WXUVCTDW1R, current_recurring_plan = 'prov', users.subscribtion = 5
    • ❌ No cc_logs row with processor paypal for that transaction
    • ❌ No cc_purchase row, no invoice PDF, no success email

Repair already done (manual)

Backfilled via php artisan paypal:backfill-payment 29546 I-E1WXUVCTDW1R (new command: BackfillPaypalPayment.php):

  • 1 cc_logs row (trxtype R, transid 1G49172999430860H, processor paypal, $75.00)
  • 1 cc_purchase row (product_id 16, profile_id I-E1WXUVCTDW1R)
  • Timestamps UTC+0, verified in DB (log_id 107574). Invoice will be auto-generated from cc_purchase.

Result — findings & remediation plan

Findings based on the original incident (user 29546):

Findings

  1. Swallowed errors in best-effort logging — insertCCPurchaseForUpgrade is wrapped in a try/catch that only does error_log("cc_purchase/invoice failed:") (UpgradeHandler.php:437-454). Any failure in cc_logs / cc_purchase / invoice generation disappears silently.
  2. Silent early-return — if billing info lookup returns empty, postUpdateBestEffort returns without any log (UpgradeHandler.php:409-411).
  3. Partial writes without rollback — core user DB is written first, transaction logging runs afterwards as best-effort, with no DB transaction and no retry. Failure mid-way produces exactly this incident: user data ✅ but cc_logs/cc_purchase ❌.
  4. No safety net after payment succeeds — refund/cancel compensation only triggers for failures before the DB update; there is no PayPal webhook or reconciliation to detect/repair gaps.

Remediation plan (separate tasks to be created)

  • Replace swallowed error_log calls with structured Log::error + alerting
  • Never silently early-return on missing billing info — at minimum log a structured warning
  • Wrap DB writes in a single transaction, or add an outbox/retry mechanism so logging gaps self-heal
  • Reconciliation cron: compare COMPLETED PayPal transactions vs cc_purchase, auto-backfill missing rows

issues.display_title: Issue #1794: Record PayPal recurring transactions cronjob
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

PayPal-equivalent of #1764: a cronjob endpoint that records PayPal recurring subscription renewal payments into the legacy billing tables, the same way RecordStripeRecurringTransactionsHelper does for Stripe.

Current state

Stripe recurring renewal charges are now logged via /record-stripe-recurring-transactions (#1764, PR #1760): each renewal charge is written to cc_logs_stripe, and a deduped cc_purchase row is inserted when the charge succeeded and a user_id was resolved. PayPal REST API subscriptions (CreateSubscription.php) have no equivalent — renewal payments on PayPal subscriptions are not being logged to cc_logs_paypal or cc_purchase anywhere in the API codebase.

Note: #1471 already tracks a broader PayPal cronjob (porting the legacy PayFlow Pro script get_paypal_link_trans.php and covering REST API subscriptions). This issue scopes out just the REST API recurring-renewal slice, mirrored 1:1 against the Stripe implementation, so it can ship independently of the PayFlow Pro migration.

Target state

  • Fetch PayPal subscription renewal payments for the cronjob window and log every attempt to cc_logs_paypal.
  • Insert a deduped cc_purchase row for successful renewals when a user_id can be resolved.
  • Resolve user_id from user_extra_data.recurring_profile / recurring_profile_photo_studio — same column Stripe uses; PayPal subscription IDs (I-...) are stored there too (see CreateSubscription.php), so the resolution tier is identical to RecordStripeRecurringTransactionsHelper::resolveUserId().
  • Resolve product_id the same way the sync PayPal subscribe flow does (PaypalHelper::convertProductNameToId() / plan-to-product mapping — check CreateSubscription.php for the exact source).
  • Dedup purchase inserts by PayPal capture/transaction id.
  • Support ?test_mode=1 against PayPal sandbox, matching the Stripe cronjob's manual-verification pattern.

Open design question — how to enumerate renewal payments

Stripe's helper does one polling call (charges.all with a created range) across the whole account. PayPal REST has no direct equivalent:

  • Option A — per-subscription polling: loop every active PayPal recurring_profile in user_extra_data, call GET /v1/billing/subscriptions/{id}/transactions?start_time=&end_time= for each. Simple, no extra scopes, but O(n) calls per run.
  • Option B — Transaction Search API: GET /v1/reporting/transactions returns all account transactions (including subscription payments) in one paginated call, closer to the Stripe charges.all shape — but requires the Transaction Search product/scope to be enabled on the PayPal app; confirm this is available before committing to it.
  • Option C — webhooks: subscribe to PAYMENT.SALE.COMPLETED / BILLING.SUBSCRIPTION.PAYMENT.FAILED and log on receipt instead of polling. Real-time, but it's a webhook handler, not a cronjob — bigger shape change from the Stripe pattern and needs its own reconciliation story for missed events.

Whoever picks this up should confirm which option is viable against the current PayPal app config before implementing.

Scope

  • routes/cronjobRoutes.php — add the cronjob route (e.g. record-paypal-recurring-transactions).
  • app/Http/Controllers/Cronjobs/CronjobController.php — wire the endpoint, following recordStripeRecurringTransactions() as the template.
  • app/Http/Controllers/Cronjobs/Helpers/RecordPaypalRecurringTransactionsHelper.php — orchestrate payment fetch, filtering, logging, user/product resolution, and purchase insert.
  • app/Http/Controllers/Cronjobs/Helpers/PaypalRecurringChargeRules.php — isolate the recurring-cycle and purchase-recording decision rules, mirroring StripeRecurringChargeRules.
  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Helpers/Paypal/PaypalHelper.php — add whatever fetch method the chosen option (A/B/C above) needs.
  • api-collection/GoThru API NEW/Cronjob/Record Paypal Recurring Transactions.yml — add Bruno/manual API entry.
  • tests/Helpers/Cronjobs/PaypalRecurringChargeRulesTest.php — cover the pure decision rules.

Out of scope

  • Legacy PayFlow Pro migration (get_paypal_link_trans.php) — tracked separately in #1471.
  • Backfilling historical recurring payments.
  • Changing existing synchronous subscribe, upgrade, downgrade, Stripe, or non-subscription purchase flows.

References

  • Stripe implementation: app/Http/Controllers/Cronjobs/Helpers/RecordStripeRecurringTransactionsHelper.php, StripeRecurringChargeRules.php (#1764, PR #1760)
  • PayPal subscription creation flow: app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Subscription/Subscription/CreateSubscription.php
  • Related broader ticket: #1471
